item.title: Minnesota tribe reduces casino land request by nearly 75% after locals raise concerns
item.description: The White Earth Nation in Minnesota has reduced its proposed casino land-trust request from nearly 300 acres to 80 following concerns about drinking water, traffic, infrastructure costs, and property taxes. The project, planned for Clay County, has not yet received federal approval and also requires concurrence from Minnesota's governor. Tribal representatives say a decision could come by late 2028 under the most favourable circumstances.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 52-acre California vineyard once part of Hollywood star Fred MacMurray’s ranch lists for $22 million
item.description: Part of Hollywood actor Fred MacMurray’s 1,750-acre California ranch, the 52-acre Flax Estate and Vineyard in Healdsburg has hit the market for $22 million. Owned by philanthropists Jeffrey and Laurie Ubben, who bought the property for $21 million in 2016, the estate features 26 acres of organically farmed Pinot Noir vineyards and three residences.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: San Francisco co-op born after Black displacement gets $23 million boost for 2,400-home redevelopment
item.description: Freedom West Homes has acquired crucial funding to embark on an ambitious redevelopment initiative that will yield 2,400 new homes. This project prioritizes the needs of existing cooperative shareholders, ensuring they remain in place rather than face displacement. Notably, it focuses on replacing dilapidated structures while maintaining ownership for Black and immigrant families.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Australia’s endangered palm cockatoos get artificial nests; first chick fledges in world-first
item.description: A palm cockatoo chick has recently fledged from an artificial hollow in the Cape York Peninsula, marking a positive step for conservationists. They installed 29 artificial nesting hollows to combat the lack of natural breeding sites. This first successful breeding event is a pivotal achievement in palm cockatoo conservation. Ongoing monitoring will assess how well these new hollows can facilitate nesting and chick growth for this endangered species.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Glacier Cliffs Retreat And Stabilise: Study tracks rapid ice loss; long-term collapse less certain
item.description: Recent research reveals that Antarctica's glaciers are retreating at a faster pace than earlier predictions had estimated. By analyzing over 15,000 satellite images, scientists focused on the stability of ice cliffs. While some cliffs showed signs of quick retreat, they later stabilized instead of collapsing completely. Factors like water depth and the shape of the underlying bedrock significantly influence glacier stability.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Rhode Island Home Price Cut: landmark Reading Room gets $1.2m trim; now listed at $9.75m
item.description: The Reading Room, a stunning waterfront residence dating back to 1880, is now available for $9.75 million, down from its original listing of $10.95 million. This beautifully restored Victorian property boasts incredible views of Narragansett Bay, allowing future owners to enjoy a unique slice of coastal heritage. Its charm and character make it an exceptional opportunity for buyers seeking a historic home.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Tyler Perry cuts Wyoming mansion price by $3.5 million after $30 million Puerto Rico home purchase
item.description: Tyler Perry has reduced the asking price of his Wyoming mansion by $3.5 million, bringing it down to $36 million after reportedly buying a $30 million home in Puerto Rico. Built in 2019, the 37-acre estate features nine bedrooms, 8.5 bathrooms, a home theatre, a cowboy-themed bar, a swimming pool and a guesthouse.

item.title: Sacramento jury awards $33.3 million to physics student injured by a falling tree branch in 2020
item.description: In a landmark decision, a jury in Sacramento awarded Michael Flynn $33.3 million after he sustained a brain injury from a dead branch falling during his jog in McKinley Park. The city was found wholly negligent in their tree maintenance and safety checks. Despite the injury, Flynn persevered through rehabilitation to earn his doctorate in physics, advocating for greater accountability in public infrastructure safety.

item.title: In Southern California, five rival supercolonies of Argentine ants are engaged in a war that has led to 15 million deaths already
item.description: A tumultuous and deadly rivalry unfolds among five Argentine ant supercolonies in San Diego, resulting in an alarming number of fatalities. These strongly territorial ants engage in relentless battles, disregarding the 'dear enemy effect' common in territorial animals. Surprisingly, studies reveal that these colonies have reached an impasse, maintaining fixed borders even amid continuous aggression, indicating a lengthy conflict without an end in sight.

item.title: Reba McEntire-backed Texas charity has welcomed over 35,000 families since 1992
item.description: Established in 1992 by Reba McEntire, Reba's Ranch House serves as a sanctuary for families of hospitalized patients, having provided aid to over 35,000 families. The house offers not just accommodation and meals but also emotional and spiritual support through initiatives like Room for Hope. Many guests have experienced marked improvements in sleep and anxiety during their stay, reflecting the house's responsive growth to community needs.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dallas’ historic theater to relight its tower after $45 million redevelopment
item.description: On November 1, Dallas's iconic Forest Theater is poised to make its grand return following significant restoration efforts. With a staggering $45 million injection aimed at modernizing its cultural offerings, the reopening promises live performances and food vendors to engage the community. The relighting of the Tower and marquee heralds a rejuvenated era, fostering support for local artists and revitalizing the South Dallas cultural scene.

item.title: London residents may keep homes after 12-year fight against estate demolition
item.description: In a pivotal decision, Lambeth Council has announced plans to halt the demolition of the Central Hill and Cressingham Gardens housing estates. The focus will shift toward improving existing homes and fostering community ties, sparing residents from the threat of eviction. This significant turnaround, subject to Cabinet approval on October 21, marks a commitment to preserve community integrity and architectural character.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: London taxi driver’s £40 painting linked to 19th-century Amritsar sells for £75,000 at auction
item.description: In a remarkable twist of fate, a British taxi driver's modest £40 purchase at a car boot sale has turned into a windfall, as the artwork, featuring the iconic Golden Temple in Amritsar, fetched an astonishing £75,000 at auction. Thought to be the work of artist Baba Bishan Singh, this event highlights the pivotal role of expert appraisals in unveiling the true worth of hidden treasures in art.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Delaware marked its state parks' 75th anniversary by planting its 75,000th tree, completing a five-year goal across 17 parks
item.description: Delaware celebrates the planting of its 75,000th tree in state parks, coinciding with the park system's 75th anniversary. This achievement contributes to a larger goal of planting one million trees by 2030. The initiative features diverse tree species, driven by the support of community volunteers. Notable trees like the American holly were chosen to improve environmental quality and provide inviting spaces for the public.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Lonnie Mack’s iconic Flying V guitar and amplifier sell for $550,000 at auction
item.description: The legendary 1958 Gibson Flying V guitar, famously owned by Lonnie Mack and dubbed 'Number 7', fetched an impressive $550,000 at auction. This auction also featured Mack's 1962 Magnatone Custom 440 amplifier, which was crucial to his distinct sound. Mack's guitar, tailored for his innovative techniques, has had a profound influence on blues-rock music for many years.
